acceptance.observable: FIRST, the planner's suspected defect: R90 may trade one invented claim for another.
At 7200e1c, closeAndRestore's R90 branch pushes an absent → unobservable (<code>) change and continues. So it neither restores nor adds anything to unrestored.
The summary sentence is chosen by unrestored.length === 0 && changes.length > 0, which prints "Every file was put back by bytes before any git call read the repository."
So when the unobservable path is the only change, the report may claim a restore that did not happen, while an unobservable file may still be in the tree.
This is a planner's READING, not a run. Reproduce it or refute it with Q130-R85-REPO-UNREADABLE-ZEROED's shape and the created-then-unlstatable shape. Report the exact message.
If it holds, it is a defect under R90's own words: "never prints invented facts". Rate its severity yourself.
